lines.trans: Hey, fool, why are you sitting here?
I am a great head chef, and not a fool at all!
Then why are you not cooking in the kitchen?
I was temporarily kicked out of my own restaurant.
Who dared to kick out such a strict cook?
One impudent woman from the neighboring restaurant.
Women always bring men big problems.
You are absolutely right, my chance interlocutor.
And what are you going to do now?
I will return and win back my kitchen!
Now those are the right words, brave cook!
Thank you for the advice, I am going to win!

meanings.note: Coordinating or subordinating Russian conjunction meaning 'and', linking clauses in spoken dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('so, and what about') (starting a question: а жвачку?) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Да это не воровство, послушай! Это абсолютно безопасно.
examples.trans: That's not stealing, listen! It's completely safe.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('big, large').

examples.text: Аракелян просит время. Сумма очень большая.
examples.trans: Arakelyan is asking for more time. The sum is very large.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('great').

вернуть.gloss: to give back, to get back

meanings.note: Russian perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to give back', forming an aspectual pair with 'возвращать'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.
Secondary conversational sense ('to get back') (money you spent) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Ты эти деньги через полгода вернёшь.
examples.trans: You'll get this money back in six months.

meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to come back, to return', paired with 'возвращаться'.

examples.text: Так, не шумим. Я скоро вернусь.
examples.trans: Right, no noise. I'll be back soon.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'at all'.

examples.text: Я вовсе не хочу спорить с вами.
examples.trans: I do not want to argue with you at all.

examples.text: Вовсе нет, я жду хозяина ресторана.
examples.trans: Not at all, I am waiting for the restaurant owner.
These are not silly jokes at all.

meanings.note: Conversational Russian particle ('here') that adds modal nuance, emphasis, or discourse tone in spoken dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('! = you'll see!') (emphasis) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: All right, here you go. There, look.

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'temporarily'.

examples.text: Меня временно выгнали из собственного ресторана.
examples.trans: I was temporarily kicked out of my own restaurant.

meanings.note: Prefix 'вс-' ('up') marks upward or sudden onset of action (stem 'егда').

examples.trans: She's offended. She's always like that.

выгнать.gloss: to kick out, to evict, to drive out

meanings.en: to kick out, to drive out
meanings.note: Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'гнать'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to kick out', forming an aspectual pair with 'выгонять'.

examples.text: Для тебя она добрая. А меня она выгонит!
examples.trans: She's kind to you. But she'll kick me out!

examples.text: Значит, меня не выгонят со службы?
examples.trans: Does that mean I won't be fired from service?

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to cook; to prepare', paired with 'приготовить'.
Secondary conversational sense ('to prepare') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Я уже не могу готовить, стирать, убирать. Я хочу на море!
examples.trans: I can't take the cooking, washing and cleaning any more. I want to go to the sea!

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to do, to make', paired with 'сделать'.
Secondary conversational sense ('to make') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Hi, Arkady Borisovich. What are you doing?

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'fool', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Костик, ты дурак! Это статусная вещь.
examples.trans: Kostik, you're a fool! This is a status piece.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'woman' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Твоя жена очень мудрая женщина. Ты её слушай.
examples.trans: Your wife is a very wise woman. You listen to her.

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'for' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('behind') (+ instrumental) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'here'.
emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to go', forming an aspectual pair with 'пойти'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.
Secondary conversational sense ('expression') (to run for a second term) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: + genitive: 'из мэрии' = from the town hall

examples.text: Марина Сергеевна, я уже знаю. Мне звонили из мэрии.
examples.trans: Marina Sergeyevna, I already know. The town hall called me.

meanings.note: in the instrumental: 'кем ты работаешь?'

examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, who are your rivals?

meanings.note: Entered Russian via Polish 'kuchnia' and Middle High German 'küchen', ultimately from Late Latin 'coquina' (from 'coquere', to cook).
Secondary conversational sense ('cuisine, cooking') (русская кухня = Russian cuisine) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Three rooms and a big kitchen.
And the kitchen is over there.

meanings.note: Russian determiner/pronoun ('my') agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun phrase it specifies.
adult male; declines like a feminine -а noun

examples.text: У мужчины бывает не только жена.
examples.trans: A man can have more than just a wife.
This man is waiting for you.

examples.text: У мужчины, мальчик, бывает не только жена. Это моя девушка.
examples.trans: A man, my boy, can have more than just a wife. She's my girlfriend.

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'on' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('onto, to; for') (+ accusative: на второй срок) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: showing a lack of respect in a rude or aggressive manner

examples.trans: That was a very insolent act.
Be quiet right now, insolent rump!

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates
agrees in gender and case with the noun
Secondary conversational sense ('alone') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'беждать'). Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to win', forming an aspectual pair with 'победить'.

examples.trans: Justice always triumphs in the end.

examples.text: Наша команда регулярно побеждает в турнире.
examples.trans: Our team regularly wins the tournament.

examples.text: Спасибо за совет, я иду побеждать!
examples.trans: Thank you for the advice, I am going to win!

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'cook', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Есть такой английский повар. Я по его передачам научусь готовить.
examples.trans: There is this English chef. I will learn to cook from his shows.

examples.text: Я хочу работать поваром в ресторане.
examples.trans: I want to work as a cook in a restaurant.

meanings.note: + infinitive; как ты посмел? = how dare you?

examples.text: Да как ты посмел? Это собака маленькой девочки!
examples.trans: How dare you! That's a little girl's dog!

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'why'.

examples.trans: Why are we going so slowly?

examples.text: Виталик, почему мы так медленно едем? Быстрее!
examples.trans: Vitalik, why are we going so slowly? Faster!

meanings.note: Qualitative or relational adjective formed with the productive '-н-' suffix, meaning 'correct' and agreeing in gender, number, and case.

examples.trans: A course of the correct antibiotics.
We have prescribed a course of the correct antibiotics.

meanings.note: Descriptive Russian adjective meaning 'right', agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies.
Secondary conversational sense ('right, correct') (short form: ты прав = you're right) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Заходите. Поставьте, пожалуйста, правую ногу на кровать.
examples.trans: Come in. Please put your right foot on the bed.

meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'носить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to bring', paired with 'принести'.

examples.text: Я приношу бутылку шампанского и свечи.
examples.trans: I'll bring a bottle of champagne and candles.

examples.text: И не надо больше никаких документов сюда приносить!
examples.trans: And don't bring any more documents in here!

meanings.note: 'будут проблемы' = there'll be trouble

examples.trans: I know the problems of ordinary people.

meanings.note: Borrowed from French 'restaurant' (from 'restaurer', to restore strength with rich broth); entered Russian in the early 19th century.

examples.text: Слушай, Нина, это же тот самый ресторан!
examples.trans: Listen, Nina, this is that very restaurant!

examples.text: Мы рады видеть вас в нашем ресторане.
examples.trans: We are glad to see you in our restaurant.
They called from the Italian restaurant.

meanings.note: refers back to the subject: 'он держит своё слово' = he keeps his word

examples.text: А что я за мэр такой, который держит своё слово?
examples.trans: And what kind of mayor would I be if I kept my word?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'идеть'). Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to sit', forming an aspectual pair with 'посидеть'.

examples.trans: Why are you sitting in the corner?

meanings.note: 'дать слово' = to give one's word, 'держать слово' = to keep one's word
'дать слово' = to give one's word, 'держать слово' = to keep one's word

examples.text: А что я за мэр такой, который держит своё слово?
examples.trans: And what kind of mayor would I be if I kept my word?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'лучайный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('accidental').

examples.trans: It was a completely accidental misunderstanding.

examples.text: Ты абсолютно прав, мой случайный собеседник.
examples.trans: You are absolutely right, my chance interlocutor.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'мелый'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('brave, bold').

examples.text: Ты какой смелый! А что ты будешь делать, если она узнает?
examples.trans: How brave you are! And what will you do if she finds out?

meanings.note: Agentive or instrument masculine noun meaning 'interlocutor', declining across all six Russian grammatical cases.

examples.text: Ты абсолютно прав, мой случайный собеседник.
examples.trans: You are absolutely right, my chance interlocutor.

собираться.gloss: to intend, to be about to; to gather

meanings.en: to intend, to plan, to be going to
meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'обираться'). Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to intend', forming an aspectual pair with 'собраться'. The reflexive suffix '-ся'/'-сь' makes the action intransitive, reciprocal, or directed at the subject.
Secondary conversational sense ('to gather, to get ready') (pack or assemble) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Ну и что? Я всё равно переезжать собираюсь.
examples.trans: So what? I'm planning to move anyway.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'обственный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('own, proper').

examples.text: Я хочу купить собственную строительную компанию.
examples.trans: I want to buy my own construction company.

meanings.note: общественный совет = public council
Secondary conversational sense ('piece of advice') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Это правильно. Я приглашаю вас в общественный совет.
examples.trans: That's right. I'm inviting you onto the public council.

meanings.note: Qualitative or relational adjective formed with the productive '-н-' suffix, meaning 'neighboring' and agreeing in gender, number, and case.

examples.text: За соседним столиком сидели приятные люди.
examples.trans: Pleasant people were sitting at the next table.
To a guest at the next table.

examples.text: В соседнем зале играет тихая музыка.
examples.trans: Quiet music plays in the neighboring hall.

meanings.note: спасибо за + accusative = thank you for

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'трогий'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('strict, stern').

examples.trans: How strict you are, Klavdia Viktorovna.

examples.text: У нас в школе очень строгий директор.
examples.trans: We have a very strict principal at our school.

examples.text: Ой, спина не разгибается! Какая вы строгая, Клавдия Викторовна.
examples.trans: Ow, my back won't straighten! How strict you are, Klavdia Viktorovna.

meanings.note: 'что я за мэр такой' = what kind of mayor am I
Secondary conversational sense ('? = what's this?') used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'now'.

examples.text: Теперь я начальник нашей стройки. Ты уволен!
examples.trans: Now I'm the boss of our building site. You're fired!

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'then'.
Secondary conversational sense ('then, in that case') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Я тебе тогда сказал: ты меня ещё поцелуешь.
examples.trans: I told you back then: you'll kiss me one day.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('you') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('what') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('that') (conjunction) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('? = well?') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.en: executive chef, head of a kitchen
meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'head chef', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.trans: The head chef developed a new menu.
She works as an executive chef in Moscow.
The head chef manages the entire kitchen.

meanings.note: Expressive conversational Russian interjection or greeting ('hey') used directly in spoken exchanges.

examples.text: Хорошая, никто же не говорит. Эй, ты что?
examples.trans: She is good, nobody's saying she isn't. Hey, what's wrong?

meanings.note: pointing at a thing or a situation; 'это' + noun = 'this is ...'
points at something: это моё = that's mine
Secondary conversational sense ('is') (linking word: главное — это народ) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.note: меня = me (genitive/accusative), мне = to me (dative)
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.
